# Capital gains on shares

Only matters outside the ISA and SIPP: the Vanguard GIA, the AJ Bell gilts (exempt) and the 140 Unilever shares Dad gave me in 2019.

## Annual exempt amount

The allowance has been cut to almost nothing:

- 2022/23: £12,300
- 2023/24: £6,000
- 2024/25 onwards: £3,000

Losses can be carried forward indefinitely if reported within 4 years. I have £1,140 of losses from the 2022 Scottish Mortgage sale, reported on the 2022/23 return, still unused.

## Rates, and the October 2024 change

From **30 October 2024** the rates on shares went from 10% / 20% to **18% / 24%**. Anything sold 6 Apr to 29 Oct 2024 is at the old rates, after that the new. The return for 2024/25 splits the year in two, so keep the dates of each disposal straight.

I'm a higher-rate taxpayer, so for me it's 20% before, 24% after.

## Section 104 pool, how I keep it

All shares of the same class in the same company are pooled. Average cost = total allowable cost / total shares. Every purchase adds to it, every reinvested dividend adds to it (relevant for the GIA, see [[Dividend reinvestment]]), every sale takes out the proportionate cost.

Matching order on a sale:

1. Same-day purchases
2. Purchases in the next 30 days (bed and breakfast rule)
3. The Section 104 pool

Spreadsheet: `CGT-Pool-2025.xlsx`, one tab per holding.

## Unilever, worked example

Gift from Dad, 18 Jun 2019. A gift is a disposal by him at market value and an acquisition by me at the same value: 140 shares at £45.93 = £6,430.20 base cost. (He was under his allowance that year so nothing to pay.)

Sold 60 shares on 14 Oct 2024 at £47.86, dealing charge £11.95.

- Proceeds: 60 × 47.86 = £2,871.60 - £11.95 = £2,859.65
- Cost: 60/140 × 6,430.20 = £2,755.80
- Gain: £103.85

Well within the £3,000. Still reported? Only if proceeds total more than £50,000 or there's a gain over the allowance, so no. Pool now 80 shares, cost £3,674.40.

## Vanguard GIA sale, December 2024

Sold £6,000 of FTSE 100 income units on 9 Dec 2024 for the bed-and-ISA (moved into the ISA in April 2025).

- Units sold: 1,331.54 at £4.5061
- Pool average cost after reinvestments: £3.9772
- Gain: about £704. Taxable rate 24% because it's after 30 Oct, but under the £3,000 allowance once added to Unilever (£103.85). Total gains 2024/25: £807.85. No tax.

Did NOT buy the same fund back in the GIA within 30 days. Buying it inside the ISA is fine, the B&B rule doesn't reach into the wrapper.

## Things that tripped me up

- Gilts are exempt but corporate bonds aren't always. Check before buying anything for the [[Bond ladder]].
- Accumulation units in a GIA: the notional distribution adds to the base cost even though no cash moved. Forgetting it means paying CGT on money already taxed as income.
- Spouse transfers are no gain / no loss. Javier has his own £3,000. Could have moved 40 Unilever shares to him before selling. Next time.

## Reporting

2024/25 return: no CGT pages needed unless the gilt sale proceeds count toward the £50k test (they don't, exempt assets). Keep everything 5 years past the filing date. Monthly regular investing in the ISA never touches any of this, see [[Index funds]] and [[定投基金笔记]].
